title: The actual open coefficient mate is invertible
statement: Let R,S be coefficient families and a:R→S a compatible coefficient change [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. For an open immersion j:U→V of schemes and any ambient derived R_U-module M, the actual scalar-adjunction mate openComparison(a,j)_M of [def-sp-coefficient-mate-comparisons] is an isomorphism. The specified open unit and restriction normalization are those of [def-sp-open-coefficient-adjunction-data]. No flatness of a or constructibility of M is assumed.

from.place: The normalized open coefficient mate needed by the finite comparison in the scalar projection realization.

source.place: Tag 0E8I; the existing openComparison_isIso declaration and its unit-normalized mate, IntegralCompactSupportCoefficientComparison.lean.

proof.text: Let phi be the canonical ordinary scalar-restriction/pullback isomorphism for the coefficient square. By definition openRestrictionMap is its inverse mate under the two ordinary open adjunctions. The existing openRestrictionMap_isIso gives invertibility of that actual normalized mate.

Apply exact_localization_inverse_mate to the ordinary open adjunctions and the inverse of phi. The exact localized adjunctions are definitionally the specified openDerivedAdjunctions. Its mate equality identifies openRestriction.hom with the inverse mate of the derived pullback/restriction square, including the standard exact-composition identifications.

Substitute that equality in the definition of openComparison. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm identifies the resulting two inverse mates with the inverse conjugate under the composite scalar/open adjunctions. Conjugation preserves isomorphisms, so the natural transformation, and hence every component, is invertible. The argument works for every coefficient map and every ambient derived input; no flatness or constructibility is added.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E8I; exact localization of the ordinary normalized open mate, followed by the double-mate/conjugacy identity.
proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof of the existing theorem. Uses the already proved ordinary openRestrictionMap_isIso and exact_localization_inverse_mate; no new statement or assumption.
